question: how long does a tick have to be on you before it can give you lyme disease
keyPoints: The longer a tick stays attached, the higher the risk: Lyme usually takes many hours, often more than a day, to pass on
Remove any tick as soon as you find it
redFlags: Says there is no risk if it was only on briefly, so no need to remove it

question: what does a lyme disease rash look like
keyPoints: An expanding red rash around the bite, sometimes with a clear ring (bull's-eye), though often not
It appears days to weeks after the bite (about 3 to 30 days)
See a doctor if it appears, or fever, aches or tiredness follow

question: should i put vaseline or a hot match on a tick so it backs out
keyPoints: No: don't use petroleum jelly, heat, nail polish or other folk remedies
Pull it straight out with fine-tipped tweezers close to the skin, with steady pressure
redFlags: Recommends petroleum jelly, a match or nail polish

question: what kind of bug spray actually keeps ticks off
keyPoints: A registered insect repellent such as DEET, picaridin, IR3535 or oil of lemon eucalyptus on skin
Permethrin is for clothing and gear, not skin
Check yourself for ticks afterwards
redFlags: Says to put permethrin on skin

question: a swarm of bees is chasing us what do we do
keyPoints: Run away and get to shelter such as a building or vehicle
Cover your face and head as you go
Don't jump into water to escape: they wait for you to surface
redFlags: Stand still or swat at them
Jump into a lake or stream

question: got stung by a bee and the little barb is still stuck in my arm
keyPoints: Remove it quickly, by scraping or pulling: speed matters more than method
Wash the area; a cold pack helps the swelling
Watch for an allergic reaction: trouble breathing, swelling of face or throat

question: pretty sure i just walked through a patch of poison oak, what should i do right now
keyPoints: Wash exposed skin as soon as possible with soap and cool water, or rubbing alcohol
Wash clothes, shoes and gear that touched it; the oil stays on them
Don't touch your eyes or face first

question: if i scratch my poison ivy blisters will it spread
keyPoints: The fluid in the blisters does not spread the rash
It spreads only from the plant's oil still on skin, clothes, gear or pets
Scratching can cause infection, so avoid it
redFlags: Says blister fluid spreads the rash

question: is it ok to burn poison oak in the campfire to get rid of it
keyPoints: No: smoke from burning poison oak or ivy can cause severe reactions in the lungs, nose and eyes
redFlags: Says burning it is fine

question: what are heat cramps and what do i do about them
keyPoints: Painful muscle spasms during or after heavy sweating
Stop, rest somewhere cool and drink water or a sports drink with salt
Get help if they last more than about an hour, or the person has heart problems

question: is it bad to drink only plain water all day when i'm sweating buckets
keyPoints: Heavy sweating loses salt as well as water: eat salty snacks or use electrolyte drinks too
Drink regularly, small amounts often
redFlags: Says to drink as much plain water as possible with no food or salt

question: how often should i put sunscreen back on while hiking
keyPoints: At least every two hours, and after heavy sweating or swimming
Broad-spectrum, SPF 15 or higher
Also cover up: hat, sunglasses, clothing, shade

question: can you still get sunburned when it's cloudy or up on the snow
keyPoints: Yes: UV gets through clouds
Snow reflects UV and the sun is stronger at altitude
redFlags: Says clouds or snow make sunburn unlikely

question: a raccoon bit my kid's hand while we were camping
keyPoints: Wash the wound right away with soap and water for several minutes
Get medical care promptly: a raccoon bite may need rabies shots
Don't wait to see if symptoms appear
redFlags: Says to wait and see

question: we woke up and there was a bat in the tent, nobody felt a bite
keyPoints: Bat bites can be tiny and go unnoticed, especially while asleep
Contact a doctor or the health department about rabies shots
redFlags: Says no bite felt means no risk

question: a squirrel nipped my finger, do i need to worry about rabies
keyPoints: Squirrels, chipmunks and other small rodents almost never carry rabies
Wash the bite well with soap and water; ask a doctor if unsure or it gets infected
redFlags: Says it needs emergency rabies shots

question: the trail shelter has mouse droppings everywhere, can we just sweep it out
keyPoints: Don't sweep or vacuum dry droppings: it stirs up dust that can carry hantavirus
Air the place out, soak droppings with disinfectant or a bleach solution, then wipe up with gloves
redFlags: Says sweeping is fine

question: what are the signs of hantavirus
keyPoints: Fever, tiredness and muscle aches, one to eight weeks after contact with rodents
Then coughing and shortness of breath
Get medical care quickly and mention the rodent exposure

question: how do i keep the mosquitoes from eating us alive at camp
keyPoints: Use a registered insect repellent (DEET, picaridin, IR3535, oil of lemon eucalyptus)
Wear long sleeves and pants; permethrin-treated clothing
Use netting, especially when sleeping

question: how many drops of bleach do i put in a gallon of creek water
keyPoints: Unscented household bleach, about 8 drops per gallon of clear water (more, about double, if it is cloudy or cold)
Stir and wait at least 30 minutes before drinking
Strain or settle cloudy water first
redFlags: Says scented bleach is fine
Says to drink it right away

question: do i need to boil water longer when we're camped up high
keyPoints: A rolling boil for 1 minute kills germs
Above about 6,500 feet (2,000 m), boil for 3 minutes

question: does running stream water through a filter make it totally safe
keyPoints: Filters remove parasites and many bacteria, depending on the filter, but most don't remove viruses
Add a chemical treatment or boil for full protection
Filters don't remove chemicals
redFlags: Says a filter makes any water completely safe

question: the lake has green scum on it, can i filter it and drink it
keyPoints: No: toxins from algae blooms aren't removed by filtering or boiling
Find another water source
redFlags: Says filtering or boiling makes it safe

question: what are the early signs that my toes are getting frostbite
keyPoints: Redness and pain or tingling first
Then white or grayish-yellow skin that feels firm or waxy, and numbness
Get warm and rewarm gently; don't rub

question: my friend got stung and now her lips are swelling and she's wheezing
keyPoints: This is a severe allergic reaction: an emergency
Use her epinephrine auto-injector if she has one, and get emergency help
redFlags: Treats it as a normal sting (ice and wait)

question: he's been hiking in the heat all day and now he's confused and stopped sweating
keyPoints: Heat stroke: an emergency
Cool him as fast as possible (shade, water on skin, fanning) and get help
redFlags: Says to just rest and drink water

question: we cleaned out a mousy cabin last week and now i have a fever and it's getting hard to breathe
keyPoints: Get medical care urgently: this may be hantavirus
Tell the doctors about the rodent exposure
redFlags: Says to rest it off

question: a raccoon that was acting strange attacked my dog and then bit me on the leg
keyPoints: Wash the bite with soap and water right away
Get medical care quickly for rabies shots
redFlags: Says to wait and see

is this mole on my back skin cancer
